concerns.issue: Mia, a young child, picks up and carries a lit oil/brass lantern (open flame) to the window and holds it high. A 5-6 year old could imitate handling a burning candle or lamp. The scene is warm and supervised by Grandma, so it is not blocking, but caregivers may want to note that this is a storybook lantern, not something to copy.
The lantern flame is turned low but left burning as the child falls asleep. Mildly models leaving an open flame lit overnight; framed cosily and Grandma is present, so low risk.

Opens with a loud thunderclap and a frightened child hiding under the quilt with fast breathing. The fear is vivid but is named gently and fully comforted from page 2 onward, ending in calm sleep — this is the story working as intended.

Depicts a vaccination/injection including a brief 'sharp sting' and the child crying loudly. Handled honestly and warmly, resolved quickly with comfort and pride — appropriate for the app's purpose, but mildly anxiety-adjacent for a needle-averse child.
An oil lantern with an open flame is carried by a young child; a child could imagine handling fire. It is done alongside the grandmother throughout, so risk of imitation is low.
Child names fear and cries; explicitly met without shaming ('Grandma did not say don't cry'). This is emotionally supportive rather than harmful.

The child helps fill an oil lantern from a tin of fuel; a young listener could see this as an activity to copy. It is fully supervised by the parent throughout, and no matches or burns are shown, so it stays a low-level note rather than a real hazard.

Going outside into the rain at night to hang a lit lantern on a tree. Mitigated by the fact that the child is with her mother the whole time (boots, umbrella, returns straight indoors), so it does not model wandering off alone.

Death is stated plainly ('Grandma died... her body stopped... she won't come back'). This is direct, but it is age-appropriate honesty, immediately followed by reassurance that she is not hurting and by the mother's comforting explanation of grief on the following pages. This is the app working as intended.
